nodes.label: A man in his 50s presented with a 5-week history of right facial paresis, facial numbness, and severe ipsilateral headaches
He presented to an outside ED shortly after onset and was treated with an unknown antibiotic without steroids; medical history included poorly controlled diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism

Physical exam showed right-sided chemosis and exophthalmos, purulent nasal secretions, maxillary nerve hypoesthesia, complete eye closure with effort, moderate brow weakness, lip droop with effort (House-Brackmann III right facial paresis), and intact left facial nerve
Nasal endoscopy revealed polypoid changes of the right middle turbinate and purulence within the nasal cavity, with no necrotic debris observed
CT shows right orbital abscess arising from rhinosinusitis with bony erosion but intact lamina papyracea
Biopsy shows chronic inflammation and fibropurulent exudate without fungus
Cultures grow coagulase-negative Staphylococcus and Enterococcus faecalis
Orbital abscess secondary to bacterial rhinosinusitis
